messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] model sample in windows, doesnt sample in linux
parts:
Nothing is platform dependent in Stan, but you have to give
us more context on what you're trying to do and what's going wrong.
It sounds like an installation problem or a problem with
how you're calling Stan.

And no, you don't ever want to create a diagonal matrix and
then multiply by a Cholesky decompsoition. It's better if
you just declare Rho as a Cholesky factor for a correlation
matrix, and then use diag_pre_multiply() to scale it by SD_fs12.

- Bob

messages.author: 82889e926eb5165e
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] model sample in windows, doesnt sample in linux
parts: Apparently the problem was due a the parametrization of the correlation. Windows and Mac allow the model to estimate with

> vector<lower=0>[2] Sd_fs12; 
> corr_matrix[2] Rho; 
> cholesky_factor_cov[2] Ly; 
> 
> Ly <- diag_matrix(Sd_fs12) * cholesky_decompose(Rho);

As I change it to 

cholesky_factor_corr[2] Ly_C;
matrix[2,2] Ly;

Ly <- diag_pre_multiply(Sd_fs12, Ly_C);

It works fine in both linux and windows.

Linux was more sensitive to the misspecification

Thank you for your help

On Wednesday, January 20, 2016 at 5:13:28 PM UTC-6, Bob Carpenter wrote:
Nothing is platform dependent in Stan, but you have to give
us more context on what you're trying to do and what's going wrong.
It sounds like an installation problem or a problem with
how you're calling Stan.

And no, you don't ever want to create a diagonal matrix and
then multiply by a Cholesky decompsoition.  It's better if
you just declare Rho as a Cholesky factor for a correlation
matrix, and then use diag_pre_multiply() to scale it by SD_fs12.

- Bob

> On Jan 19, 2016, at 6:23 PM, Mauricio Garnier-Villarreal <mauga...@gmail.com> wrote:

> Hi
>
> When I try to print Rho and cholesky_decompose(Rho) linux doesnt pirnt it, only prints the same error messages.
>

>
> In windows I use the compiler by Rtools
>

> vector<lower=0>[2] Sd_fs12;
> corr_matrix[2] Rho;
> cholesky_factor_cov[2] Ly;
>
> Ly <- diag_matrix(Sd_fs12) * cholesky_decompose(Rho);

>
>

>
>
> On Tuesday, January 19, 2016 at 4:45:26 PM UTC-6, Bob Carpenter wrote:
> It may also be an initialization issue.  We've seeen that
> before.
>
> The C++ spec is rather vague in many points (or should I
> say, "platform dependent").  So you're not guaranteed to get
> the same output even for different levels of optimization on
> the sample platform and with the exact same compiler.
>
> - Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] model sample in windows, doesnt sample in linux
parts:
It's not so much Windows vs. Mac as most likely differences
in machine bit size (is one 32 bit and the other 64 bit),
CPU (same CPUs?), and compiler (even the same compiler on different
optimization levels can give you different results).

There's a chapter on replication in the manual that's basically
a list of everything that can go wrong. The only way to get
reliable replication is to lock down everything (hardware, OS
version, compiler version, compiler flags).

- Bob
